examples.ko: 화장품 견본품을 받아서 먼저 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I got a sample of the cosmetics and tried it first.
This product is a sample, so it isn't for sale.
A sample is placed at the entrance of the store.

examples.ko: 견본품과 실제 상품의 색이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: The color of the sample differs a little from the actual product.
This sample is free, but please take only one.
Before signing the contract, we checked the quality with a sample.

explain: 일상에서는 '샘플'이라고 많이 말하고, '견본품'은 안내문이나 서류, 상품 설명에서 쓰는 느낌이에요. 매장에 진열해 놓은 물건이나 계약 전에 확인하려고 만든 물건에 잘 어울려요. '견본품 표시'처럼 팔지 않는다는 표시로도 써요.

phrases.example: 화장품 샘플을 받아서 먼저 써 봤어요.
phrases.en: I got a cosmetics sample and tried it first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '견본품' 대신 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word people use most often instead of 견본품.

phrases.example: 상자에 견본품 표시가 있어서 살 수 없어요.
phrases.en: The box is marked as a sample, so I can't buy it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔지 않는 물건이라는 것을 알리는 표시로, 안내문에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: A label saying the item is not for sale, often seen on notices.

phrases.en: The store gives out samples for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상점이나 행사에서 손님에게 주는 상황에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits shops or events handing samples to customers.

explain_en: In daily talk people say '샘플', while '견본품' feels like the word for notices, documents and product descriptions. It suits display items in a store or items made to check before a contract. It also appears as a mark saying the item is not for sale.

t90.ax: This sample is free, but please take only one.

examples.en: I rent a bicycle when I travel.
You need a membership card to rent comic books at a rental shop.
There's a shop nearby that rents out suits.

examples.ko: 차를 대여하고 제주도를 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: I rented a car and drove all the way around Jeju.
Could I rent a camera for just one day?
You have to return rented items on the due date.

explain: 친구에게 빌릴 때는 '빌리다', 빌려줄 때는 '빌려주다'를 쓰고, '대여하다'는 가게나 서비스에서 값을 내고 빌리거나 빌려줄 때 써요. 돌려주는 일은 '반납'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I borrowed an umbrella from my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람끼리나 일상에서 빌릴 때는 '대여하다'보다 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 대여하다 for borrowing in daily life or from a person.

phrases.example: 자전거 대여료는 한 시간에 삼천 원이에요.
phrases.en: The bicycle rental fee is 3,000 won per hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 빌릴 때 내는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The money you pay to rent something.

phrases.en: I have to return the borrowed book by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대여한 물건을 돌려줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving back something you rented or borrowed.

explain_en: Between friends you say 빌리다 (borrow) and 빌려주다 (lend). 대여하다 is for renting from or to a shop or service for a fee. Returning the item is 반납.

t90.ax: I rent a bicycle when I travel.

examples.en: I pick up my parcels at the security office.

examples.ko: 상품을 수령한 뒤에 후기를 남겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please leave a review after you receive the product.
I receive my salary on the 25th of every month.

examples.ko: 대리인이 서류를 대신 수령할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A representative can receive the documents on your behalf.
There is a problem with the item I received yesterday.
I went up on the stage to receive the award.

explain: '받다'의 딱딱한 말이에요. 택배, 서류, 급여처럼 공식적인 것에 쓰고, 친구에게 선물을 받을 때는 '받다'를 써요. 명사 '수령'은 '우두머리'라는 다른 말도 있어서 문장을 보고 구분해요.

phrases.en: I received the package at the security office.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수령하다'의 쉬운 말로 일상 대화에서 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plain word for '수령하다', used widely in daily talk.

phrases.en: Please pick up the documents at the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 직접 가서 받아 가라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to tell people to come and pick something up.

phrases.en: I receive my pay on the 25th of every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 급여처럼 공식적인 것을 받을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for formal things like money or pay.

explain_en: It is the formal counterpart of '받다'. Use it for official things such as parcels, documents and pay; for a gift from a friend, use '받다'. The noun '수령' can also mean a leader, so tell them apart from the sentence.

dis.h: official; take delivery of items or money
gh: accept applications or documents at a desk

p.n: 받다 is casual; 수령하다 sounds formal or like a receipt.

t90.ax: I pick up my parcels at the security office.

examples.en: I picked a sofa after looking at the furniture catalog.
The new catalog arrived by mail.

examples.ko: 이 카탈로그에는 신제품이 다 나와 있어요.
examples.en: All the new products are in this catalog.
You can also download the catalog online.

examples.ko: 카탈로그 속 사진이 너무 예뻐서 샀어요.
examples.en: The photo in the catalog was so pretty that I bought it.

examples.ko: 카탈로그로 비교해 보니 가격 차이가 컸어요.
examples.en: Comparing them in catalogs, the price difference was big.

explain: 종이 책자뿐 아니라 파일로 된 것도 카탈로그라고 불러요. '카탈로그를 보다', '카탈로그를 받다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: There are many new products in the product catalog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파는 물건이 담긴 카탈로그를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A catalog that lists items for sale.

phrases.en: I picked clothes I liked from the catalog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 물건 중에서 하나를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing one item among many.

phrases.en: I ordered a catalog to be sent to my home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받고 싶은 카탈로그를 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when requesting a catalog to be sent.

explain_en: Not only paper booklets but also files are called this. You look at it or receive it.

examples.en: Please tell me where this product is sold.
You can only buy it at official retailers.
There are so few retailers that it is hard to find.
I looked for online sellers, but everything is sold out.
The seller's address is written on the package.

examples.ko: 새 책이 나와서 판매처가 늘어날 거예요.
examples.en: The new book is out, so the number of retailers will grow.

explain: 판매처는 광고나 상품 설명에서 '어디서 살 수 있는지'를 안내할 때 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '어디서 팔아요?'라고 더 많이 해요. 사는 사람 쪽에서는 '구입처'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: It's safe to buy from an official retailer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 인정한 가게나 사이트를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for stores or sites approved by the company.

phrases.en: I'm looking for where this product is sold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사려는 사람이 어디서 파는지 알아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a buyer tries to find where something is sold.

phrases.en: If you tell me where you bought it, I'll give you a refund.
phrases.nuance_ko: '판매처'는 파는 쪽, '구입처'는 산 곳이라는 점이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: '판매처' is from the seller's side; '구입처' is the place you bought from.

explain_en: 판매처 often appears in ads and product pages to say where something can be bought. In speech people usually ask '어디서 팔아요?' instead. From the buyer's side, '구입처' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: The factory processes meat.

examples.ko: 사진을 가공해서 색을 더 밝게 만들었어요.
examples.en: I edited the photo to make the colors brighter.

examples.ko: 우리는 우유를 가공해 치즈를 만들 거예요.
examples.en: We will process milk to make cheese.
Nutrients decrease during processing.
Processed food is easy to store.
After processing the raw materials, we put them in boxes.

explain: 원재료나 자료를 손질해서 다른 상태로 만들 때 써요. '가공식품'은 이미 손질해서 파는 음식이고, 사진을 보정할 때도 '가공했다'고 해요. '가공의 인물'에서 쓰는 '가공'은 지어낸 이야기라는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Don't eat too much processed food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손질해서 파는 음식을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for food that has been processed before being sold.

phrases.en: An edited photo is different from the real color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 손질하거나 보정한 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies the noun that follows. Refers to something treated or edited.

phrases.en: This fruit is processed into juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원재료가 다른 상태로 만들어지는 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the result of raw material being made into something else.

explain_en: Used when raw materials or data are worked into another form. '가공식품' is processed food, and editing a photo can also be '가공하다'. The '가공' in '가공의 인물' (a fictional person) is a different word meaning made up.

examples.en: The teacher proctors the exam.
That person directed the movie.
I work supervising a construction site.

examples.ko: 부모님이 숙제를 감독하면 아이가 더 열심히 해요.
examples.en: When parents keep an eye on homework, kids work harder.
Tomorrow I'll oversee it myself.

examples.ko: 축구팀을 감독한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's been five years since I started coaching the soccer team.

explain: 사람이나 일이 규칙대로 되는지 지켜보고 이끄는 일이에요. 영화에서는 '영화를 감독하다', 운동에서는 팀을 이끄는 사람을 '감독'이라고 불러요. 사람을 부를 때는 '감독님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The teacher supervises the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 때 규칙을 지키는지 지켜보는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use: watching that exam rules are followed.

phrases.en: The team leader oversees the construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 잘 되는지 지켜보고 이끄는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means watching over and directing how work is going.

phrases.en: The coach spoke to the players.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동팀이나 영화의 감독을 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to address a sports coach or film director.

explain_en: It means watching and guiding people or work to see that things go by the rules. For films it means directing. In sports the head of a team is called a '감독'. When addressing the person, say '감독님'.

examples.en: The school posts the test results on the notice board.
I posted the notice on the website.
Get permission before you post a photo.
We need a place to put up the notice.
I want to delete the post I made.
I put the closing day on the shop door and left work.

explain: 누구나 볼 수 있게 게시판이나 웹사이트에 올려 두는 일에 써요. 온라인에서는 '올리다'가 일상적이고, 게시하다는 공지·규정 같은 공식 글에 더 어울려요. 올라온 글은 '게시글', '게시물'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The test results are posted on the website today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올라가는 결과에 초점을 둔 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on what gets posted.

phrases.en: Please read the post carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게시판에 올라온 글을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A written post on a bulletin board.

phrases.en: Posts that break the rules are deleted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글뿐 아니라 사진이나 영상도 포함해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Includes photos and videos as well as text.

explain_en: It is for putting something on a notice board or website where anyone can see it. Online, '올리다' (upload) is the everyday word, and 게시하다 fits official posts such as notices and rules. A posted item is called '게시글' or '게시물'.

examples.en: I sent my cover letter enclosed with my résumé.
I enclosed one photo in the letter.
I forgot to enclose the application form.
I have enclosed the contract, so please check it.
Please sign the enclosed documents and send them back.

examples.ko: 소포에 영수증을 동봉해 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you enclose the receipt in the package?

explain: 편지나 소포 안에 다른 것을 함께 넣는다는 뜻이라 격식 있는 글에 잘 나와요. 이메일에서는 '첨부하다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Please check the enclosed document and sign it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 넣은 것을 가리킬 때 '동봉한'으로 꾸며 써요. 편지나 공문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point to something already enclosed, with 동봉한 modifying the noun. Common in letters and official documents.

phrases.en: I'll enclose a thank-you card in the package.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이나 손님에게 무엇을 함께 넣어 보내겠다고 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell a superior or customer that you will put something in together with the item.

phrases.en: I forgot and didn't enclose the receipt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넣지 못했거나 넣는 것을 잊었을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used when you did not or forgot to include something in the envelope or package.

explain_en: It means putting something else together inside a letter or package, so it fits formal writing well. For email, people more often say '첨부하다'.

t90.ax: I enclosed one photo in the letter.

en: to hand out; to distribute (copies to each person)

examples.en: The teacher handed out the test papers to the students.

examples.ko: 회의 전에 자료를 미리 배부해 주세요.
examples.en: Please hand out the materials before the meeting.
The district office hands out trash bags for free.
They are handing out notices at the event hall.
They lined people up to hand out masks.
They didn't hand out the materials, so I didn't know the content.

explain: 여러 사람에게 서류나 물건을 나눠 줄 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '나눠 주다'가 더 자연스러워요. 학교, 회사, 관공서 안내문에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: The teacher handed out printouts to the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배부하다'와 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 배부하다 but more natural in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The notice was distributed to all the students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-되다'를 붙인 피동 형태로 누가 나눠 줬는지보다 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form with '-되다' that focuses on the result rather than who handed it out.

phrases.en: The city hall distributed masks for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공공기관이나 단체가 공짜로 나눠 줄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when public offices or groups give things out for free.

explain_en: It is a formal word for giving out documents or items to many people. In everyday talk, '나눠 주다' sounds more natural. You often see it in notices from schools, companies and government offices.

examples.en: Please give me one copy of the contract.
I'll keep the original and give you just a copy.
I made a copy of the file and edited it.
I need a copy of the passport.
This copy is as clear as the original.
Don't stamp the copy.

explain: 반대말은 '원본'이에요. 종이를 복사기로 뽑은 것도, 컴퓨터 파일을 복제한 것도 '복사본'이라고 해요. 서류를 낼 때는 '사본'이라는 말도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: Please submit a copy of your ID too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 낼 때 '복사본' 대신 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used instead of 복사본 for documents.

phrases.en: Make a copy of important files.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 파일을 복사해 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when copying paper or files.

phrases.en: I saved a copy of the photos on a USB drive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터 파일을 복제해 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when keeping a duplicate of a computer file.

explain_en: The opposite is '원본'. Both a photocopy and a duplicated computer file are called '복사본'. When submitting documents, '사본' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I'll send you the contract by email.

examples.ko: 계약서 송부 일정을 확인하고 싶은데 담당자께 문의해도 될까요?
examples.en: I'd like to check the schedule for sending the contract. May I ask the person in charge?
One document is missing from the list of papers to send.
The documents haven't been sent yet.

examples.ko: 자료를 먼저 송부하신 뒤에 전화 주세요.
examples.en: Please call me after you send the materials first.

examples.ko: 어제 송부한 파일이 열리지 않는다고 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a message that the file I sent yesterday won't open.

explain: '보내다'의 업무용·공문서 말투예요. 서류, 자료, 계약서처럼 격식 있는 물건에 쓰고, 친구에게 사진을 보낼 때는 '보내다'가 자연스러워요. 메일이나 공문에서 '송부드립니다'로 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I will send you the materials by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업무 메일이나 전화에서 정중하게 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely promise something in work emails or calls.

phrases.en: I received the documents yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 쪽에서 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the receiving side in a formal way.

phrases.en: I sent the photo to my friend right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말로, 격식 없는 상황에 알맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word, suitable for informal situations.

explain_en: It is the business and official-document version of '보내다'. It is used for formal items such as documents, materials and contracts, while sending a photo to a friend sounds natural only with '보내다'. You'll often see it in emails and notices as '송부드립니다'.

t90.ax: I'll send you the contract by email.
